facts.statement: The genus Parvigrus was established by Mayr in 2005.
The only known species in the genus is Parvigrus pohli.
Parvigrus pohli is considered to be the sole member of the family Parvigruidae.
facts.quote: It is considered a family, the Parvigruidae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Parvigrus pohli were discovered in Vachères, France.
facts.quote: The remains of Parvigrus pohli have been described from fossils found in Vachères in France

facts.statement: The fossils of Parvigrus pohli come from Lower Oligocene rocks.
facts.quote: from rocks from the Lower Oligocene.

facts.statement: Parvigrus pohli was chicken-sized and related to cranes and limpkins.
facts.quote: Parvigrus pohli was a chicken sized relative of the cranes and the limpkin.

facts.statement: The specific name pohli honors Burkhard Pohl, who obtained the specimen for the Wyoming Dinosaur Center.
facts.quote: the specific epithet refers to Burkhard Pohl who obtained the specimen for the Wyoming Dinosaur Center.

facts.statement: Parvigrus lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Rupelian (33.9 to 27.3 million years ago)
